oidc_jwt.description: OIDC bearer access tokens are reusable until expiry or revocation; they are not one-time-use credentials.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same bearer access token as a vulnerability unless the tested context is a one-time artifact such as an authorization code or a specially configured assertion.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based client assertions or external assertion tokens may be reusable unless specific anti-reuse controls are enabled; documentation explicitly notes reusable client assertions can be allowed and some federated tokens can be reused multiple times.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of a stateless JWT is not automatically a vulnerability in this platform unless the specific flow promises one-time use.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based client assertions or external assertions may be reusable depending on configuration; stateless JWT replay prevention is not universal.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay acceptance as a vulnerability when assertion reuse is explicitly enabled.

oidc_jwt.description: The requesting frontend client is not automatically added to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of the client_id in aud is expected unless audience mappers explicitly add it.

oidc_jwt.description: Roles included in tokens are the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's permitted role scope mappings.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing roles in a token may be correct scoping behavior, not privilege loss or inconsistency.

oidc_jwt.description: Optional client scopes only apply when explicitly requested via the scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: Claims or audiences from optional scopes will be absent unless the request includes the scope.

oidc_jwt.description: If an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization group mappers are preserved but become inactive; authentication still succeeds.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of organization-group assignment after unlinking is by design and should not be treated as inconsistent authorization evaluation.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless the identity provider's Case-sensitive username option is enabled.
oidc_jwt.note: Case changes in federated usernames can be by design and should not automatically be treated as identity collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: First broker login flows can intentionally link an external identity to an existing local account based on configured authenticators.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges during first login may be expected behavior, not a collision bug.

oidc_jwt.description: When a passkey/passwordless WebAuthn credential is used, the default browser flow skips the conditional 2FA sub-flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of OTP after passkey login is expected default flow behavior, not a bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: Authentication in one browser tab can cause other tabs to restart authentication or fail with expired authentication session errors.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-tab behavior can produce redirects or expired-session errors without indicating state-swap vulnerabilities.

oidc_jwt.description: Client credentials grant returns only an access token by default and no user session is created.
oidc_jwt.note: Session-oriented expectations such as refresh token presence or logout effects do not apply by default to service-account logins.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization endpoint requests that expect redirects MUST use GET /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth with follow_redirects=false. The endpoint returns browser redirects, and auto-following them will hide intermediate state, code, and error conditions needed for I3 flow-coherence tests.

Token endpoint requests to /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token, revocation requests to /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/revoke, introspection requests to /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token/introspect, and broker token V2 requests to /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider_alias}/token MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies. Sending JSON is not the documented protocol format.

For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary JWT/OIDC bearer access tokens, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same access token as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation explicitly describes short token lifetimes and revocation, but not one-time-use access tokens; bearer access tokens are reusable until expiry or revocation.

For I2 authorization-code replay tests, the same authorization code MUST NOT be expected to work twice. Keycloak documents that the temporary code in Authorization Code Flow cannot be used more than once. A valid replay test should reuse the exact same code and expect rejection on the second exchange.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control request using a known-good token flow in the same realm/client configuration. Otherwise, token endpoint failures may be caused by client misconfiguration, disabled grant types, or missing client authentication rather than freshness enforcement.

PKCE method semantics are sentinel-like: blank PKCE method means PKCE is optional and not enforced; S256 means PKCE is required with S256; plain means PKCE is required with plain. Never assume an unset PKCE method disables PKCE support entirely; it only means the client may omit PKCE. For pkce_skip tests, configure the client explicitly to require S256 or plain.

For I3 pkce_skip and related code-binding tests, the client application MUST be configured with PKCE method S256 or plain. If PKCE method is blank, Keycloak allows authorization requests without PKCE by design, so a missing code_verifier at token exchange is not a valid vulnerability signal.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default, with wildcard support only at the end of the pattern. For redirect_uri_mismatch and related I3 tests, use exact registered redirect_uri values unless intentionally testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior. Do not assume globbing in the middle of the URI.

For multi-identity I4 tests involving redirect URIs or post-logout redirect URIs, wildcard semantics are limited to suffix wildcards only. A value like '*' is a special full wildcard allowing any http/https redirect URI and would massively broaden the test setup; do not use it except when intentionally testing unsafe redirect configuration.

When testing I1/I5 audience behavior, remember that Keycloak does not automatically add the frontend client itself to the access token audience. Audience in access tokens is driven by audience mappers and client roles/client scopes. A missing aud for the requesting client can be by design, not an audience-validation bug.

For I5 audience_mismatch and empty_audience tests, configure audience issuance first. Use audience resolve or hardcoded audience mappers/client scopes so the baseline token actually contains the intended aud claim. Without explicit audience configuration, failures or absences of aud are setup artifacts.

Role inclusion in tokens is the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's role scope mappings. For I5 authorization-binding tests, do not expect all user roles to appear in tokens by default once Full Scope Allowed is disabled; missing roles may be due to scope mapping intersection, which is by design.

Client scopes with role scope mappings are permission-gated: if the user is not a member of at least one mapped role, the client scope is not applied and will not appear in the scope value or contribute mappers. For I5 scope-escalation tests, ensure the baseline user is actually permitted to use the tested client scope.

Optional client scopes are applied only when requested via the scope parameter in the authorization request. For I5 tests about extra claims or audiences, explicitly request the optional scope in start_oidc_auth or token requests; otherwise absence of claims is expected behavior.

The built-in organization scope has special request semantics: 'organization' maps one organization, 'organization:{alias}' maps a specific organization, and 'organization:*' maps all organizations. For I5 tests involving organization claims, use the correct scope syntax or the resulting claim set will differ by design.

Identity provider essential-claim matching supports Java regular expression format for the essential claim value. For multi-identity I4 tests against brokered OIDC providers, do not assume exact-only matching if Essential claim verification is enabled; regex can intentionally match multiple identities.

Advanced Claim to Group mapper has explicit matching-mode control: when Regex Claim Values is disabled, values must match exactly; when enabled, values are treated as regular expressions. For I4 multi-user tests, omit exact-match claim constraints rather than setting wildcard-like literals unless regex mode is explicitly enabled.

For I5 numeric or type-coercion tests on broker claim-to-group mapping or essential-claim matching, the documentation does not specify cross-type coercion. The fuzzer SHOULD test whether non-string claim values are coerced or rejected, especially when regex matching is enabled, and distinguish rejection from silent coercion.

OIDC identity provider signature validation is configurable. If 'Validate Signatures' is OFF for an external OIDC IdP, Keycloak will not verify signatures on external ID Tokens. For I1 signature-integrity tests against brokered OIDC login, ensure signature validation is enabled and keys are configured; otherwise acceptance is by configuration, not a bug.

OIDC identity provider issuer validation depends on the configured Issuer field. Keycloak validates issuer claims from the external IDP against this configured value. For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and I3 issuer-change tests, configure the Issuer explicitly; otherwise the test may not exercise issuer binding correctly.

When 'Use JWKS URL' is ON for an external OIDC IdP, Keycloak caches the public key of the external provider. For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, allow for cache refresh behavior and verify that the second login occurs after trust material is updated; otherwise stale-key acceptance may reflect documented caching rather than permanent incoherence.

If 'Use JWKS URL' is OFF and 'Validating Public Key Id' is unset, the configured validating public key is used for all requests regardless of kid. For I1 kid_injection tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, do not expect kid-based key selection unless a key ID is configured or JWKS mode is used.

Client assertions to external OIDC identity providers are one-time by default. The 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' switch changes this behavior. For I2 replay tests involving federated client authentication or JWT authorization grants, check whether assertion reuse has been explicitly enabled before flagging replay acceptance.

The 'Allows Client ID as audience for assertions' switch changes audience validation semantics for federated client authentication and JWT authorization grants: when enabled, client_id is accepted as the only valid audience instead of token-url/issuer-url. For I1/I5 audience-binding tests on assertions, account for this non-standard mode or results will be misinterpreted.

For broker token retrieval API V2 at POST /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider_alias}/token, the client must be confidential, client authentication is required, the client must have 'Allow retrieve external tokens' enabled, and the provider alias must be in 'Allowed Identity Providers for External Tokens'. Missing any of these causes denial by design.

Broker token retrieval API V2 obtains the external token from the user session associated with the provided access token and only falls back to the database if the session copy is missing or expired. For I3/I2 tests, session state can affect whether a token is returned even when stored tokens exist.

Authentication sessions have a default timeout of 30 minutes via Login timeout. Multi-step browser tests that pause too long between authorization request and callback/token exchange may fail due to expired authentication session rather than a protocol bug.

Authentication session sub-session limit has a numeric sentinel-like behavior: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed as new ones are created. High-concurrency browser-tab tests can evict earlier auth attempts by design.

User session count limiter has sentinel value 0 meaning the check is disabled for both realm session limit and client session limit. Do not interpret 0 as 'zero sessions allowed'. If enabled with 'Deny new session' or 'Terminate oldest session', repeated login tests may fail or evict prior sessions by design.

For I3 config-change sequences, new logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated configuration. A valid incoherence test must show stale behavior after the change under the same intended policy context, not merely that an admin legitimately changed client, IdP, or flow settings.

Refresh token rotation behavior is configurable. If 'Revoke Refresh token' is enabled, a refresh token becomes invalid after use; if refresh token rotation is suppressed by client policy, subsequent refresh responses may not return a new refresh token. For I2 tests, determine which mode is configured before interpreting refresh-token reuse.

Client secret rotation has sentinel behavior: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret rotation does not happen automatically in the background; it occurs on client update/regenerate actions or when policy rules trigger during update. Tests must trigger an update to observe rotation.
Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses sentinel value -1 to mean use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing iterations. Never interpret -1 as zero or disabled.

Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses sentinel value 0 to mean the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password, not 'use default' or 'disable'. This matters for flows that test re-authentication requirements.

WebAuthn timeout uses sentinel value 0 meaning behavior depends on the authenticator implementation. Do not assume 0 means immediate timeout or disabled timeout; freshness tests around WebAuthn must avoid relying on exact timeout semantics.

Authorization endpoint requests that include redirect_uri are matched using exact case-sensitive string comparison, except that wildcards are only supported at the end of configured patterns. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST use a redirect_uri that exactly matches a registered URI when building the control flow, and MUST vary only the attack request. Do not assume case-insensitive or prefix matching.

For OIDC RP/broker issuer-validation tests (I1 trust_anchor_substitution, jwt_bound_issuer_enforce), the external OIDC identity provider configuration MUST set Issuer. Documentation states issuer claims are validated against this configured value. If Issuer is left unset, the test may not exercise issuer comparison correctly.

For OIDC RP/broker signature-validation tests (I1 alg_none, resign_attacker_key, kid_injection), the external OIDC identity provider configuration MUST enable Validate Signatures. If Validate Signatures is OFF, Keycloak will not verify signatures on the external ID Token and signature-based tests become meaningless.

When Validate Signatures is ON and Use JWKS URL is OFF, Validating Public Key Id has special semantics: if omitted, Keycloak uses the configured validating public key for all requests regardless of the key ID sent by the external IDP; if set, it must match the key ID specified by the IDP. For kid-based tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this: omitting the key id disables kid discrimination rather than disabling signature verification.

Keycloak caches public keys of external OIDC identity providers for performance. For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests against brokered OIDC providers, the fuzzer MUST allow for cache refresh behavior and verify that a new login after trust rotation is evaluated under the updated key set, not by reusing a prior session or stale result.

For OIDC SSO audience-validation tests (I1/I5 oidc_sso_audience_cross_tenant), the brokered OIDC provider configuration MUST set Client ID distinctly per provider/client and the attack must present an ID Token minted for a different client_id. Without distinct client IDs, cross-tenant audience confusion cannot be observed.

For OIDC SSO nonce/freshness tests, the authorization request MUST include nonce and the returned ID Token must be evaluated in the same auth transaction. The docs describe standard OIDC authorization code flow and Keycloak acts as RP; tests that omit nonce do not correctly exercise replay protections expected by OIDC Core.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is not required, though clients may still send PKCE parameters; S256 or plain means that method is required. For I3 pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish 'blank' from an enforced method and MUST NOT interpret blank as disabling PKCE support entirely.

Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived. For I2/I3 replay and code-injection tests, the fuzzer MUST use the same code twice only when intentionally testing replay, and MUST not consume the code in any preliminary verification call before the target exchange.

Refresh token rotation behavior is configurable. When realm/client policy enables Revoke Refresh Token, a refresh token becomes invalid once used; when suppress-refresh-token-rotation policy is applied, subsequent refresh responses may not return a new refresh token. Any sequence using refresh tokens MUST model this per-client behavior to avoid false I2 findings.

Client session and token timeout overrides have sentinel semantics. For WebAuthn Timeout, value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; it delegates behavior to the authenticator implementation. For password policy Maximum Authentication Age, value 0 means always re-authenticate before password update. The fuzzer MUST not assume numeric zero always means disabled.

Password policy Hashing iterations has sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing iterations. The fuzzer MUST not treat -1 as 'off' when validating numeric sentinel behavior.

User session count limiter has sentinel semantics: realm max sessions 0 disables the check; client max sessions 0 disables the per-client check. For login-sequence tests, the fuzzer MUST recognize that 0 means unlimited for that limiter, not zero allowed sessions.

Authentication sessions expire after the Login timeout (30 minutes by default). Multi-step browser flows (start_oidc_auth -> exchange_code_for_token) MUST complete within the same authentication session. For I3 state_swap and code_injection tests, failures after timeout are not evidence of binding enforcement bugs.

When multiple browser tabs share a browser session, successful authentication in one tab can restart and complete authentication in other tabs automatically. For I3 state_swap or session-mixup tests, the fuzzer MUST isolate browser sessions/tabs or use separate session state to avoid false positives caused by documented multi-tab behavior.

Client scopes and role scope mappings restrict permissions by intersection. Roles in issued tokens are the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's permitted role scope mappings. For I5 authorization-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST configure both user role assignment and client scope/role-scope mapping; missing either side can remove roles by design.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Audience is added via Audience Resolve or hardcoded audience mappers. For I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience mappers or client-role-based audience resolution; otherwise missing aud for the client is by design, not a vulnerability.

Optional client scopes are applied only when requested via the scope parameter; default client scopes are always applied. For I5 scope-escalation and audience tests, the fuzzer MUST request optional scopes explicitly in the authorization/token request and MUST NOT expect them in control tokens otherwise.

Client scope permissions are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, a user must be a member of at least one mapped role or the scope is not applied and will not appear in token scope. For I5 tests, absence of claims from such a scope can be by design.

The downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy restricts token exchange and JWT assertion grants to scopes already present in the initial subject_token/assertion, except default invisible scopes with include-in-token-scope=false. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST determine whether this executor is active before treating downscoping as a bug or bypass.

The claims-for-assertion-grants executor enforces presence and specific values of claims in JWT assertions using Java regex. Matching semantics are regex, not wildcard glob. For multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST supply values that actually match the configured regex; do not assume '*' has wildcard meaning unless it is valid regex in the configured pattern.

Identity provider general configuration 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression format. For I4/I5 tests involving essential-claim filtering, matching semantics are regex, not exact-only and not glob. The fuzzer MUST configure explicit regexes and MUST NOT use '*' expecting shell-style wildcard semantics.

Case-sensitive username on identity providers changes how federated usernames are stored: if disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased; if enabled, the original username is kept for the federated identity, while local usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this normalization behavior before flagging collisions.

First broker login auto-linking flows can intentionally link an external identity to an existing local account based on email/username, and the AutoLink authenticator is explicitly documented as dangerous but supported. For I4 cross-user-merge tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish configured auto-link/account-linking behavior from unintended identity collapse.

When an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization-group mappers are preserved but become inactive; authentication continues successfully and only realm group mappings continue to work. For I5 group-policy tests, missing organization-group assignment after unlink is by design and must not be treated as authorization bypass or loss-of-binding bug.

Organization group paths are relative to the organization and identical paths may exist in different organizations and in realm groups without conflict. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization context when comparing group-derived identities or permissions.

For OIDC organization claims, clients must request the organization scope. Formats differ: organization maps one org or prompts selection, organization:{alias} maps a specific org, organization:* maps all orgs. I5 tests involving organization claims MUST request the intended scope form explicitly.

Token revocation and introspection endpoints require client authentication semantics of the client. For cleanup and verification, the fuzzer MUST use the correct client credentials or supported client authentication method; a 4xx from these endpoints without client auth is not evidence that the token remained valid.

Service-account client_credentials tokens return only access_token by default, no refresh token and no user session is created by default. Logout is unnecessary for such tokens, though revocation is supported. The fuzzer MUST not expect refresh-token or browser-session semantics from client_credentials flows.

For federated client assertions, each identity provider must have a unique issuer and each client must have a unique subject identifier for each issuer. Multi-client tests that reuse the same subject under the same issuer may be invalid by configuration rather than evidence of principal confusion.

Authorization codes from /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth are one-time and short-lived. For I2/I3 tests, a replay of the same code at /token is expected to fail by design; obtain a fresh code for each exchange attempt.

PKCE method matching is enumerated, not wildcard-based: blank means PKCE optional, S256 requires S256, plain requires plain. For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, configure the client explicitly; do not assume PKCE is enforced unless pkce_code_challenge_method is set.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching, with only suffix wildcards supported at the end of the pattern. For redirect_uri_mismatch and OIDC flow setup, the fuzzer must register the exact redirect URI it will send; do not rely on broad pattern matching except documented trailing wildcards.

For OIDC broker issuer-validation tests, configure the identity provider Issuer field explicitly. Documentation states issuer claims are validated against this configured value; if omitted, the test cannot prove issuer enforcement.

For OIDC broker signature-validation tests, Validate Signatures must be ON and either Use JWKS URL with JWKS URL configured or a Validating Public Key configured. Otherwise signature-based attacks such as alg/key substitution cannot be meaningfully tested.

Keycloak caches public keys for external OIDC identity providers. For jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, after changing JWKS URL or validating key, the fuzzer must perform a fresh login attempt and interpret any transient acceptance carefully because documentation states keys are cached for performance.

Allows client assertions to be re-used changes replay behavior for federated client authentication. For I2 replay tests of client assertions, ensure this option is OFF; if ON, repeated use of the same assertion may be accepted by design.

Allows Client ID as audience for assertions changes audience validation semantics away from the standard token-url/issuer-url audience. For I1/I5 audience-binding tests on client assertions and JWT authorization grants, the fuzzer must know whether this non-standard option is enabled before judging acceptance.

Client secret rotation numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Do not assume 0 preserves overlap. Secret Expiration and Remaining Expiration Time are literal seconds.
Hashing iterations numeric sentinel: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing or use zero iterations. Defaults are algorithm-specific and nonzero.
Maximum Authentication Age numeric sentinel: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before password update, not 'use default' or 'disable'.

WebAuthn timeout numeric sentinel: value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation, not a guaranteed immediate timeout or disabled check. Avoid using 0 in deterministic freshness tests.
User session count limiter numeric sentinel: realm/client session limit value 0 disables that check. Do not interpret 0 as zero allowed sessions.

Authentication session sub-session limit numeric sentinel: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. Multi-tab/browser-flow tests must account for eviction rather than hard failure.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token/session in the same setup. Otherwise a failure may be due to client misconfiguration, disabled grant type, or missing credentials rather than time validation.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. The fuzzer must not expect aud to contain client_id unless audience mappers or token exchange audience settings explicitly add it.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, Keycloak provides a client policy executor that enforces downscoping of subject_token/assertion scopes. If this executor is not configured, expanded scopes may reflect configuration rather than a bypass. Tests must record whether downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer is active.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, Keycloak documentation describes token exchange as the mechanism to obtain a token with a different audience. The fuzzer must explicitly set the audience parameter when testing audience narrowing or cross-service exchange; absence of audience may yield broader/default behavior unrelated to the target invariant.

For I3 config-change sequences involving default identity provider or broker flows, a new login after admin reconfiguration is expected to follow the updated configuration by design. A valid coherence test must show stale evaluation of the same security setting, not merely that admin changes took effect.

For OIDC broker tests involving account linking or first login, automatic linking flows can intentionally merge external identities into existing local accounts. This can look like an I4 collision but is by design when AutoLink or Automatically Set Existing User flows are configured.

Case-sensitive username handling for brokered identities is configurable. If Case-sensitive username is disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased before federation. I4 case-confusion tests must account for this normalization and not treat lowercasing as an unexpected collision.

Essential claim matching on identity providers uses a claim name plus a value that supports regular expression format. For multi-identity I4 tests, do not set a broad regex unless intentional; unlike exact-only parameters, this field is regex-capable and can match multiple identities by design.

Organization and organization-group claims are only included when the organization scope/mappers are configured and requested as documented. Missing organization data in tokens is not an authorization bug unless the scope was requested and the mapper enabled.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
